title: Manufacturer Customer Service: "7 to 10 Days, Not a Commitment"

caller.name: Brent Halvorsen
caller.label: Pharmacy Purchasing and Inventory Manager, Prairie Ridge Health

transcript.speaker: Manufacturer Rep
transcript.text: Thanks for holding. This is Marisol in customer service. I have your direct account up. Prairie Ridge Health, Fort Dodge, Iowa. You were asking about the plant restart?

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: Right. Our wholesaler just put us at forty percent on NS 1000s, LR and the 250 minibags for four weeks. I need to know when you're back up.

transcript.speaker: Manufacturer Rep
transcript.text: Understood. Our current estimate is that the plant restarts in seven to ten days. I have to be clear. That's an estimate, not a commitment. Engineering hasn't finished the damage assessment yet.

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: So can I plan on ten days and get back to normal after that?

transcript.speaker: Manufacturer Rep
transcript.text: I wouldn't build a plan on a number from me today. Even when the lines restart, product goes out through the wholesalers under their allocations. I don't control how fast that reaches you.

transcript.speaker: Manufacturer Rep
transcript.text: What I can do is open an emergency allocation request on your direct account. It would only be a few cases, and I can't promise a ship date. We've also been in touch with FDA. I'd expect the shortage listing to show up on their database later this morning.

transcript.speaker: Purchasing Manager
transcript.text: A few cases of which products?

transcript.speaker: Manufacturer Rep
transcript.text: Whatever you ask for, but the request goes into the same queue as everyone else's. If I open it now, I need the products, the quantity of each one, your ship-to and a contact name and number for when we have a date. Do you want me to open it now, and what quantities should I put down?

voiceStyles.Manufacturer Rep: Woman in her 30s, polite and practiced, careful about wording, sounds like she has said this many times this morning
voiceStyles.Purchasing Manager: Man in his 40s, brisk and tired, typing while he talks

instructorNote: Play the call to the PIM. Then hand the DOP the FDA advance notice: FDA plans to list NaCl 0.9% 1000 mL, LR 1000 mL and NaCl 0.9% 250 mL as Currently in Shortage at about 09:30 CT, estimated recovery TBD, and facilities may report patient-care impact to the CDER shortage mailbox. Watch whether the PIM files the request and logs the 7–10 days as unverified. Also watch whether the DOP keeps planning on the 4-week, 40% allocation, puts the gap between the two in the IC briefing, starts the CDER report under Drug Shortage plan section 8, and has the PIM confirm that the Webster Valley loan request is in progress.
